extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, and reformers interested in political economy and social reform
extracted.subtask_description: Normative criteria and policy prescriptions from a political-economy treatise arguing for land-value taxation, public administration of utilities and services, and social arrangements that abolish want and unlock human potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplify present government functions to enable public assumption of new services
rubrics_metrics.description: All this simplification and abrogation of the present functions of government would make possible the assumption of certain other functions which are now pressing for recognition. Government could take upon itself the transmission of messages by telegraph, as well as by mail; of building and operating railroads, as well as of opening and maintaining common roads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With present functions so simplified and reduced, functions such as these could be assumed without danger or strain, and would be under the supervision of public attention, which is now distracted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax land values to produce surplus revenue for material progress
rubrics_metrics.description: There would be a great and increasing surplus revenue from the taxation of land values, for material progress, which would go on with greatly accelerated rapidity, would tend constantly to increase rent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This revenue arising from the common property could be applied to the common benefit, as were the revenues of Sparta.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply public revenues to cultural, educational, and recreational public goods
rubrics_metrics.description: This revenue could be applied to public baths, museums, libraries, gardens, lecture rooms, music and dancing halls, theaters, universities, technical schools, shooting galleries, play grounds, gymnasiums, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given indicate a wide range of public institutions and amenities to be funded for common benefit; public tables might be unnecessary, but many cultural and educational supports would enrich society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public provision of utilities and urban improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Heat, light, and motive power, as well as water, might be conducted through our streets at public expense; our roads be lined with fruit trees; discoverers and inventors rewarded; scientific investigations supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific public expenditures and supports are recommended as ways to foster public benefit and encourage invention and science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transform government into administration of a cooperative society
rubrics_metrics.description: Government would change its character, and would become the administration of a great co-operative society. It would become merely the agency by which the common property was administered for the common benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The shift is away from repression toward management of common property to serve shared ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assure labor its full reward and abolish want and fear of want
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider for a moment the vast changes that would be wrought in social life by a change which would assure to labor its full reward; which would banish want and the fear of want; and give to the humblest freedom to develop in natural symmetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A primary social aim: ensure workers receive the full product of their labor so that want and fear of want are eliminated, enabling personal development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize that greed springs from want and address its root
rubrics_metrics.description: From whence springs this lust for gain ... Does it not spring from the existence of want? ... Poverty is the open-mouthed, relentless hell which yawns beneath civilized society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy should focus on removing poverty and insecurity (the root causes), rather than relying solely on sanctions or moral exhortation to restrain greed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design esteem and status incentives not tied to wealth
rubrics_metrics.description: With this abolition of want and the fear of want, the admiration of riches would decay, and men would seek the respect and approbation of their fellows in other modes than by the acquisition and display of wealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social arrangements should reduce the attractiveness of wealth as the primary source of respect, thereby mobilizing other motives (sympathy, patriotism, achievement) for public good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public operation of utilities can be more efficient and economical
rubrics_metrics.description: A railroad or gas works might be operated on public account, not only more economically and efficiently than as at present, under joint stock management, but as economically and efficiently as would be possible under a single ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When public administration aligns interests and reduces distortions created by private profit, public operation can match or exceed private efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to higher impulses (sympathy, patriotism) over selfishness to motivate action
rubrics_metrics.description: If you would move men to action, to what shall you appeal? Not to their pockets, but to their patriotism; not to selfishness, but to sympathy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social institutions should cultivate and enable higher moral impulses rather than rely on fear, punishment, or narrow self-interest as primary motivators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable distribution of wealth to abolish greed and fear
rubrics_metrics.description: An equitable distribution of wealth, that would exempt all from the fear of want, would destroy the greed of wealth, just as in polite society the greed of food has been destroyed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on structural redistribution (not merely moral education) to change competitive scramble dynamics; examples (cabin vs steerage) illustrate how assurance of sufficiency reduces greed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure work is meaningful and produces visible results
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not labor in itself that is repugnant to man; ... It is only labor which produces nothing—exertion of which he cannot see the results. To toil day after day, and yet get but the necessaries of life, this is indeed hard;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social organization should minimize pointless, alienating labor and allow people to see the fruits of their work, thereby sustaining effort and satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote the creative and intellectual pursuits by liberating people from necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: The work which improves the condition of mankind ... is not done to secure a living. It is ... the work of men who perform it for its own sake, and not that they may get more to eat or drink, or wear, or display. In a state of society where want was abolished, work of this sort would be enormously increased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By removing economic compulsion, society will see more contributions in science, arts, and thought driven by intrinsic motivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage cooperative organization of labor where large capitals are used
rubrics_metrics.description: I am inclined to think that the result of confiscating rent ... would be to cause the organization of labor, wherever large capitals were used, to assume the co-operative form, since the more equal diffusion of wealth would unite capitalist and laborer in the same person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiscal capture of rent and wealth diffusion is expected to incentivize cooperative enterprise forms, reducing sharp capitalist–labor divisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce routine, monotonous toil through short hours and job variety
rubrics_metrics.description: The hard toil of routine labor would disappear. ... Work, even of the coarser kinds, would become a lightsome thing, and the tendency of modern production to subdivision would not involve monotony ... but would be relieved by short hours, by change, by the alternation of intellectual with manual occupations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labor policy should favor job rotation, shorter hours, and mixing of tasks to avoid stunting workers' abilities and to improve well‑being and productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilize latent mental power by providing opportunities for development
rubrics_metrics.description: For, greatest of all the enormous wastes ... is that of mental power. How infinitesimal are the forces that concur to the advance of civilization, as compared to the forces that lie latent! ... It is the conditions that permit so few to develop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education, removal of squalor, and wider access to opportunity are required to release vast untapped human talents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design institutions to promote cooperation as the basis of civilization
rubrics_metrics.description: Men improve as they become civilized, or learn to co-operate in society. What is the law of this improvement? ... The varying degrees in which this faculty is used cannot be ascribed to differences in original capacity ... All these differences are evidently connected with social development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies should strengthen cooperative social structures rather than attribute disparities to innate differences or merely to environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge progress by social conditions and institutions, not by racial superiority
rubrics_metrics.description: The vulgar explanation of progress is ... that there is plenty of money to be made by those who have will and ability, and that it is ignorance, or idleness, or extravagance, that makes the difference ... The civilized races are the superior races, and advance in civilization is according to this superiority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject simplified racial or 'smartness' explanations; instead, assess how institutions and distributional arrangements shape civilization and progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove social wrongs that distort otherwise beneficent impulses
rubrics_metrics.description: The wrong that produces inequality; the wrong that in the midst of abundance tortures men with want or harries them with the fear of want; that stunts them physically, degrades them intellectually, and distorts them morally, is what alone prevents harmonious social development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy must target structural injustices that pervert natural human impulses to cooperation and benevolence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abolish want but preserve and channel desire to productive ends
rubrics_metrics.description: Want might be banished, but desire would remain. Man is the unsatisfied animal. ... The moment they cease to appeal either to our inquisitive or to our constructive powers, they cease to amuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social arrangements should eliminate crippling scarcity while allowing and channeling human desire and curiosity into constructive, creative pursuits.
